_comment: klt erc supply spec for bandgap_top -- the structural power-delivery
read T1 item 11 requires (klayout-tools docs/design-evidence-tiers.md,
item 11 'Power delivery (structural)'; gf180-bandgap#192).
bandgap_top is an ANALOG block, so item 11's Analog column applies: this
spec's run, plus item 4's own LVS report having actually carried the
supply nets in its net_correspondence. It does -- see ../erc/README.md,
'The LVS half of item 11'. The Digital column's klt place-and-route
power.pdn / power.tapcell_master / power_connectivity requirements do not
apply: there is no P&R step and no standard-cell library in this flow.
Run it (the committed report under reports/bandgap_top/ is this exact
invocation's output):
python3 layout/erc/run_erc.py
# equivalently, by hand:
klt erc layout/bandgap_top/bandgap_top.gds \
layout/erc/erc-supply-spec.json --format json
== stackup ==
Every GDS layer number below was read from the PDK's own layer table,
~/.ciel/gf180mcuD/libs.tech/klayout/tech/gf180mcu.lyp (open_pdks
f6eeac7dad085ffcc829ccfd721f7b4ce39edcf7), AND cross-checked against
klayout-tools' curated gf180mcu deck layer table
(src/klayout_tools/decks/gf180mcu.py, LAYER_NAMES + the module
docstring's layer list). They are NOT copied from another PDK's spec --
gf180mcu's numbering shares nothing useful with sky130's.
- Poly2 30/0, role 'gate'. klt erc's own contract: stackup[0] MUST carry
role 'gate', so the accumulation starts at poly, not at Metal1.
- active_layer Comp 22/0 (stackup[0] only). This makes gate area
poly n diff rather than raw poly area (klayout-tools docs/cli/erc.md,
'Gate area'). It matters here and is not boilerplate: this block draws
65 ppolyf_u + 1 ppolyf_u_1k poly resistor bodies and a poly trim
ladder -- real poly, over field, with no gate oxide and therefore no
antenna mechanism at all. Without active_layer they are counted as
gates; with it they drop out (measured on this GDS: gate_count 11 -> 10,
and the vref trim-ladder net leaves gates[] entirely).
- Metal1 34/0 .. Metal5 81/0 are the full 5LM gf180mcu conductor stack.
The supply itself is routed on Metal1 (device-row rails and tap/guard
straps), Metal2 (the vdd/vss spines) and Metal3 (over-the-cell row
rails) -- see layout/README.md 'Routing style' and #175. Metal4/Metal5
carry the MIM capacitor's bottom/top plates
(cap_mim_2f0_m4m5_noshield). They are declared anyway, and must be:
klt erc traces connectivity over EXACTLY the layers this spec names, so
omitting a level the supply can reach through would silently cut the
graph there and could split a rail that is physically whole.
== label_layer ==
Metal1_Label 34/10 is declared, and it is the ONLY label_layer declared,
because it is the only text-bearing layer this block's merged GDS
actually has. Verified against this GDS rather than assumed: `klt layers`
reports 34/10 with 3 shapes and no 36/10, 42/10, 46/10 or 81/10 at all,
and those 3 shapes are exactly the texts 'vdd', 'vss' and 'vref'.
Declaring Metal5_Label 81/10 (which a PDN-bearing digital block would)
would be inert here -- this block has no PDN and no top-level supply pin
text.
== vias ==
Contact 33/0 and Via1..Via4 (35/0, 38/0, 40/0, 41/0) bridge consecutive
stackup roles. All five are drawn in this GDS (klt layers). gf180mcu's
Via3 is 40/0 and Via4 is 41/0 -- NOT in metal order, which is exactly the
kind of transcription trap the two independent cross-checks above exist
to catch.
== nets ==
- vdd / vss, kind 'supply'. This is what makes a vdd-vss short report as
the severe erc.supply_short rather than the general
erc.multiply_driven_net, and it is what arms erc.unconnected_net for
them. erc.unconnected_net fires on ZERO matching islands (nothing in
the layout carries that label) AND on MORE THAN ONE (the rail is split
into pieces that never touch), so zero findings of that rule is
precisely the 'each supply resolves to exactly one electrical island'
verdict item 11 asks for -- not a mere absence.
- vref, kind 'signal'. Not a supply and not required by item 11; declared
because it is the block's one other labelled net, so a vdd/vref or
vss/vref short would surface as erc.multiply_driven_net instead of
going unlooked-for. Free extra coverage, no effect on the item-11
verdict.
- vsubs is deliberately NOT declared. It is a real pin of the extracted
netlist, but it exists only as klt extract's deck-synthesized substrate
net (the LVS report says so itself, twice, as device.body_unverified
warnings) -- no text on 34/10 names it. Declaring it would produce a
guaranteed erc.unconnected_net about a missing LABEL, which says
nothing about whether the substrate is tied. See README.md, 'What is
NOT verified here'.
== no ties[] ==
There is deliberately NO ties[] section, and that is a recorded tool gap
rather than an oversight. Declaring one collapses this layout into a
single electrical island and reports a FALSE erc.supply_short --
klayout-tools#2169, first isolated in gf180-drone-fc's FRICTION F-034 on
a routed standard-cell design, and reproduced here on a hand-drawn
analog one by erc-tie-spec.known-gap.json + its committed report.
Because ties[] is omitted, erc.missing_tie is NOT COMPUTED by this run
(klayout-tools docs/cli/erc.md: 'Omitted entirely -> erc.missing_tie is
never computed'). Its zero count in the committed report is an ABSENCE
OF EVIDENCE, not evidence of absence, and must never be cited as a
well-tie verdict. README.md's 'What is NOT verified here' names what does
stand in for it, and how far that substitute actually reaches.
